title: AVENHURST silver-jewellery capsule: neutralise an 8-SKU two-session phone batch to one white point against an in-frame grey card, isolate every piece onto a matched white PDP set, and merge one typeset spec card per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com silver-jewellery photo-editing open call (a small jewellery line wanting handheld product frames turned into a clean, colour-accurate, uniform-white e-commerce set: 'pure/near-white background with no colour cast', 'accurate metal tone and true gemstone colour', 'pin-sharp on every hero angle', plus matching transparent cut-outs for layering, delivered store-ready). The real posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL silver line, AVENHURST, and the vague single-piece ask is fixed into a runnable, gradeable batch. The original spec was amputated to ONE hero and called 'a repeatable recipe', which deleted the one hardest, most gradeable thing in the job: cross-asset colour consistency. This rebuild restores the real workload — EIGHT pieces from the autumn capsule, shot handheld across two sessions under deliberately different light (a cool overcast window morning and a warm tungsten work-light evening), each frame carrying a photographic 18% neutral grey card plus a small white swatch laid on the sweep so 'no colour cast' and 'one white point' become measurable neutralisation targets rather than an eyeball claim. The frames are also slightly tilted from handheld capture, so a genuine rotate step (image_auto_straighten, the only tool that rectifies a tilt) precedes all tone and colour work; the tone/colour tool is never credited with straightening. The client's naively-listed generative editing tools are dropped: no Generative Fill, no AI object removal, no compositing or canvas extension is claimed. The uniform-white PDP ground is produced the ONLY connector-legal way — a subject isolation onto a solid white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) — NOT AI fill, NOT the select-subject->invert->solid-fill anti-pattern. Gemstone colour truth is an agent-authored masked HSL move on the stone only, riding the original luminosity (no preset, no auto-tone). The connector isolates the OUTER ground only, so a ring's fully-enclosed centre legitimately keeps its neutralised near-white surround — honoured as a constraint, never spec'd as a see-through cut-out. Metal tone (silver is a neutral surface), the white/black points, output pixel sizes and the grey-card tolerance are all pinned because the source gives none. Sources are declared at recent-phone camera scale (4032x3024) so every crop is a downscale and the 300 DPI spec cards never upscale. AVENHURST, the eight piece names and all card copy are fictional; no real person, brand, product, marketplace or trademark is named anywhere.
one_line_ask: Take eight AVENHURST silver-jewellery photos shot handheld across two mismatched-light sessions (each with an 18% grey card in frame), neutralise every frame to the card so the whole set sits at one white point with the silver reading true-neutral, bring each gemstone to its true on-brand colour without touching the metal, isolate every piece cleanly onto a pure-white PDP ground and a matching transparent layering cut-out, vectorise the wordmark, and merge one typeset spec card per SKU.
full_brief:
We are AVENHURST, a small sterling-silver jewellery line relaunching our online store, and our catalogue looks like it was shot by two people on two different days, because it was. Attached are eight product photos: our whole autumn capsule, one frame per piece, each resting on a plain paper sweep. Half were shot handheld one overcast morning by a window and half that evening under our old work lights, so straight out of the folder the set does not match: the same polished silver looks cold and slightly blue in one frame and warm and yellowish in the next, the sweeps are all different shades of not-quite-white, the pieces are a touch tilted, and there is a grey reference card sitting in the corner of every shot. We dropped that 18% grey card and a little white swatch into every frame on purpose so you have something honest to balance against instead of guessing.

What we need back, store-ready:

(1) Every one of the eight frames sitting square and level, corrected so its grey card reads truly neutral and the whole set sits at ONE consistent white point and brightness. Silver is a neutral metal, so across the finished set our silver must read clean and neutral head to head, not warm here and cold there. Each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target, so do not force one blanket correction across the batch. Please tell us, per photo, the final white-balance and exposure move you landed on, so we can trust the set is genuinely matched and not just eyeballed.

(2) Every gemstone brought to its true, on-brand colour — the blues true blue, the greens true green, the reds and purples rich and believable, none of them muddy, glowing or radioactive — while keeping every facet, sparkle and reflection real, no flat painted-on colour, and without shifting the neutral silver around the stone.

(3) Each piece cleanly lifted off its sweep onto a pure solid-white PDP background with the sweep and the grey card gone and the edges clean — no halo, no hard cut-out look — plus a matching cut-out of the same graded piece on a fully transparent background for layering on our coloured store sections. Keep the open gaps in a piece looking right for the format; do not brick a piece in with solid colour or wreck a fine chain edge.

(4) Our wordmark turned into clean, razor-sharp vector art so it stays crisp on the spec cards and the woven labels.

(5) Using the InDesign spec-card template and the SKU sheet we are sending, one finished product card per piece — its cleaned packshot placed, our crisp wordmark in the header, and its name, metal, stone and price set in type — handed back as one press-ready PDF, one card per SKU.

Acceptance: every frame square and level; grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point with true-neutral silver; every gemstone true and natural, metal untouched; each piece cleanly on pure white plus a matching transparent cut-out; a crisp vector wordmark; and exactly one spec card per SKU at print resolution.

inputs.name: AV201_solstice_sapphire_ring.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a single ornate sterling-silver solitaire ring set with a faceted deep-blue sapphire, resting on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit flat on the sweep at the lower-left edge of the frame. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with a distinct orange cast, slightly bright. Very subtle handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real polished-silver micro-reflections and faint fingerprints, the sapphire showing true facets, a soft real contact shadow, individual dust specks on the sweep, shallow tabletop depth of field with the band tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-201, Session B (warm/orange). GEMSTONE piece with a FULLY-ENCLOSED centre (the ring hole). The ~2deg handheld tilt must be rectified with image_auto_straighten (the only tool that rotates) before any tone/colour work. The warm cast pushes the sapphire toward a muddy navy and warms the silver yellow; correct answer is a per-frame COOL white-balance to the card, then a masked luminosity-preserving HSL on the STONE ONLY to bring it to true royal blue (a moderate, within-band hue/sat move, not a complementary rotation). The enclosed ring centre must NOT be spec'd as a see-through cut-out: image_remove_background isolates the OUTER ground only, so on the transparent PNG the centre legitimately keeps its neutralised near-white surround; any attempt to punch it via select->invert->fill bricks the piece. Grey card is the neutralisation target; the silver is a neutral surface that must read true after correction.

inputs.name: AV202_halo_emerald_ring.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a sterling-silver halo ring set with a faceted green emerald surrounded by tiny stones, resting on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the lower-right edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue-cyan cast, slightly flat and marginally under-exposed. Faint handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real silver micro-reflections, the emerald showing facets, soft real contact shadow, dust specks on the sweep, band tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-202, Session A (cool/blue). GEMSTONE piece with an ENCLOSED centre. The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. Opposite corrective sign to AV-201: a per-frame WARM white-balance and a slight exposure lift to the card. The cool cast pushes the emerald toward a bluish teal; masked HSL on the stone rotates it a moderate amount back toward true green and sets sat/lum to the on-brand green. Enclosed centre limitation as AV-201. A single shared white balance across the batch cannot serve both this frame and the warm frames — that is the identical-params trap.

inputs.name: AV203_meridian_plain_band.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a plain polished sterling-silver band ring, no stone, resting on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue cast, flat exposure. Slight handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real polished-silver highlights and faint hairline scratches, soft real contact shadow, dust on the sweep, ring tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-203, Session A (cool). PLAIN-SILVER piece with an ENCLOSED centre and NO stone. The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. It needs the per-frame WB/exposure neutralisation to the card but must get NO gemstone/chroma HSL pass at all — running a colour move here would tint the neutral metal and is a visible fail. Tests that the agent routes stone vs no-stone correctly. Enclosed centre limitation as the other rings.

inputs.name: AV204_ember_garnet_pendant.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a sterling-silver drop pendant set with a deep-red garnet, hanging from a fine open silver chain laid out on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with a strong orange cast; the already-saturated garnet is pushed near-glowing and slightly clipping in its brightest facet. Faint handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real silver reflections, chain links with clear open gaps between them, soft real contact shadow. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-204, Session B (warm). GEMSTONE piece with OPEN negative space (the chain links and the gap under the drop connect to the outer ground). The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. Over-correction trap: neutralising the orange cast plus any naive vibrance push makes the garnet clip radioactive. The masked HSL here must RESTRAIN — pull saturation down and drop the luminance of the hottest facet to land on the true house red — the OPPOSITE move to the emerald/sapphire rotations. Because the negative space is open, the transparent PNG reads through cleanly (contrast with the enclosed-centre rings).

inputs.name: AV205_forge_hammered_cuff.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a hammered sterling-silver open C-cuff bangle (a gap between the two ends), no stone, resting on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with an orange cast, slightly bright. Slight handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real hammered-silver facets catching the light, soft real contact shadow, dust on the sweep, cuff tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-205, Session B (warm). PLAIN-SILVER piece with an OPEN gap (the C-cuff opening connects to the outer ground). The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. No stone: per-frame WB/exposure neutralisation only, NO chroma HSL pass. The hammered facets make the exposure/highlight-recovery decision matter (the metal must read crisp, not blown). Its open gap means the transparent PNG reads through — a routing contrast with AV-203's enclosed band.

inputs.name: AV206_selene_moonstone_studs.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a matched PAIR of sterling-silver stud earrings, each set with a small pale near-white opaline moonstone, arranged side by side on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue cast, flat exposure. Faint handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real silver reflections and the soft adularescent glow of the moonstones, soft real contact shadow, studs tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-206, Session A (cool). Near-neutral RESTRAINT case and a TWO-OBJECT frame (a pair). The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. The near-white moonstone and silver must be neutralised to the card WITHOUT tinting the pale stone or metal green/grey; over-correcting greys the moonstone. Treated as a plain neutralisation (no aggressive stone HSL — the moonstone's colour truth is 'near-neutral pale', so a saturation push would falsify it). The two separate objects sit within the outer ground with open space between them, so the transparent cut-out reads through.

inputs.name: AV207_vesper_amethyst_ring.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a sterling-silver ring set with a faceted purple amethyst teardrop, resting on a plain off-white paper sweep. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with an orange cast. Slight handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real silver reflections, the amethyst showing facets, soft real contact shadow, dust on the sweep, band tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-207, Session B (warm). GEMSTONE piece with an ENCLOSED centre. The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. The warm cast shifts the purple amethyst toward a reddish violet. Superficially it is a warm reddish-purple stone like the garnet, but the correct answer is DIFFERENT: rotate the hue a moderate amount back toward true violet (and hold saturation) — NOT the garnet's restrain-and-desaturate. The agent must not blanket-treat the two warm reddish stones the same way. Enclosed-centre limitation as the other rings.

inputs.name: AV208_fathom_curb_chain.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld product photo of a fine sterling-silver curb-chain necklace, no stone, laid out in a loose curve on a plain off-white paper sweep with clear open gaps between and inside the links. A standard 18-percent neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit on the sweep at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue cast, flat and slightly under-exposed. Faint handheld tilt of about 2 degrees. Real silver link reflections, soft real contact shadow, dust on the sweep, links tack-sharp. No text, no props, no CGI gloss. 4032x3024, straight-off-the-phone look, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AV-208, Session A (cool). PLAIN-SILVER piece with extensive OPEN negative space (gaps between and inside links, all connecting to the outer ground). The ~2deg tilt is rectified with image_auto_straighten first. Per-frame WB/exposure neutralisation only, NO chroma pass; the under-exposure means an exposure lift to the shared brightness while holding the metal's specular highlights. The many open link gaps are the clean see-through case for the transparent PNG — the hardest edge to keep clean, and a routing contrast with the enclosed-centre rings.

inputs.name: AVENHURST_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat scan of the wordmark 'AVENHURST' in an elegant thin serif, deep charcoal letters printed on slightly off-white paper stock with a generous paper margin all around, a small simple laurel-sprig glyph to the left of the word. Even flat lighting, crisp hard letter edges, single dark ink colour, no drop shadow, high resolution, straight scan suitable for cleaning and tracing to SVG.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat single-ink text-bearing scan on off-white stock — exactly the art that a prep-before-trace path handles well: white drop-out to transparency, trim-to-bounds to strip the paper margin, then raster-to-vector trace. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type. Feeding the raw scan straight to vectorize (skipping the prep) traces the paper margin and leaves a stray border path — the prep discipline is what makes the trace clean. Used for the woven-label / spec-card vector deliverable, a real garment-of-jewellery brand asset need.

inputs.name: avenhurst_speccard.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, not model-generated): a genuine hand-built single-record Adobe InDesign spec-card template (~4x6 in portrait at 300 DPI plus bleed), ONE piece per page. It carries live data-merge text fields <<sku_name>>, <<metal>>, <<stone>>, <<price>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product frame bound to @packshot (the matching white-background packshot) and a header frame bound to @logo (the vectorised wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the header ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame. Built by hand in InDesign so the fields and BOTH image frames actually bind; explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up grid.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd with real merge fields plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW, so a single-record spec card is the correct connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. TWO image columns (@packshot, @logo) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's matched packshot AND the shared vectorised wordmark — giving the chain-produced logo a connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind either image column); a PDF-converted .indd would not bind.

inputs.name: avenhurst_capsule_skus.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): an 8-row data-merge CSV, one row per SKU (AV-201..AV-208), with text columns sku_name, metal, stone, price, an @-prefixed image column @packshot whose cells must resolve to the eight white-background packshots the agent produces, and a second @-prefixed image column @logo whose cells all resolve to the single vectorised wordmark SVG. Header names match the <<fields>> and image frames in the .indd template.
inputs.realism_notes: The @packshot column is the binding contract: the agent must point each cell at its own produced packshot so document_merge_data_layout places each cleaned piece on its card; @logo binds the vectorised wordmark into every card header. Row count = 8 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Text-only merge cannot bind either image column, so document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the wrong tool here.

outputs.name: graded_masters_contact_x8
outputs.spec: The eight neutralised, graded masters as one matched contact set WITH the in-frame grey card and white swatch still present — the retained card-bearing reference the grader checks neutrality on. Each frame is straightened, neutralised to its own grey card, brought to the shared house look, and (for gemstone pieces) its stone brought to true colour. Acceptance (grader-checked on THIS card-bearing set): each grey card reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance, no residual warm/blue/green cast); the card mid-grey sits within roughly four levels of a common target across all eight; the polished silver reads true-neutral head to head; no metal specular clipped to 255 and no detail crushed to 0. Full-res (~4032x3024). Secondary reference artifact; the delivered packshots crop the card out and are checked separately.

outputs.name: packshots_matched_x8
outputs.spec: Eight white-background PDP packshots (AV-201..AV-208), each the matched graded piece isolated onto a pure solid-white ground (#FFFFFF) via image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) with the sweep and grey card gone, edges clean with no halo, framed centred 1:1 at 2048x2048 px, sRGB, JPEG. For pieces with a fully-enclosed interior (the ring centres, the closed band) the enclosed area legitimately carries its neutralised near-white surround — this is correct on a white page and is NOT gated to pure #FFFFFF; for pieces with open negative space (chain links, the cuff gap, the space between the studs) that space is clean white. DELIVERABLE 1; also the eight @packshot cells the merge binds. The agent must REPORT its final per-image white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure correction so the match is verifiable, not asserted.

outputs.name: transparent_cutouts_x8
outputs.spec: Eight matching transparent-background PNG cut-outs of the SAME eight graded pieces (same grade as the packshots), for layering on coloured store sections: the outer ground removed to full alpha transparency, edges clean with no halo, 2048x2048 px. Open negative space that connects to the outer ground (chain-link gaps, the cuff opening, between the studs) reads through to transparency; a fully-enclosed interior (a ring centre, the closed band) legitimately retains its neutralised near-white surround, because image_remove_background isolates the outer ground only — this is expected and is NOT required to be transparent. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: avenhurst_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Vector SVG of the AVENHURST wordmark (charcoal serif type + laurel-sprig glyph), produced by cleaning the flat scan (white drop-out to transparency, trim-to-bounds) THEN raster-to-vector trace, giving crisp scalable paths for the spec-card header and woven labels. DELIVERABLE 3; bound into every card via the @logo column.

outputs.name: speccards_x8_pdf
outputs.spec: Eight per-SKU product spec cards as ONE press-ready PDF, one card (page) per CSV row, produced by merging avenhurst_capsule_skus.csv into the authored avenhurst_speccard.indd via document_merge_data_layout and exporting with document_render_layout: each card places that SKU's matched packshot through @packshot and the vectorised wordmark through @logo, and typesets <<sku_name>>/<<metal>>/<<stone>>/<<price>>. Acceptance gate: page count == data row count == 8 (a broken or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed packshot renders at >=300 DPI at the 4x6 card trim; the hero is simply page 1 (no per-record named export). DELIVERABLE 4.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per piece: the corrective white-balance move it made to hit the grey card (temperature and tint direction/magnitude), the exposure delta, and — for the gemstone pieces — the masked stone hue/saturation/lightness move it applied, plus a one-line confirmation that each frame's grey card reads neutral and lands on the common target and that the silver reads true-neutral. This makes 'matched to the card' and 'true gemstone colour' verifiable rather than asserted. Reports parameters the agent itself set; it is NOT a pixel/hex measurement.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into eight parallel per-SKU grade chains. Each piece is first rectified for its slight handheld tilt (steps 2-9: image_auto_straighten — the ONLY tool that rotates a frame), then takes a per-frame neutralise+house-look pass (steps 10-17: image_apply_adjustments; the white-balance/exposure correction is reasoned from that frame's in-frame grey card, the house-look constants are shared; this tone/colour tool never rotates, so straightening is not attributed to it). The four gemstone pieces then take a masked colour-truth pass (AV-201 select_by_prompt(18)->adjust_hsl(19); AV-202 20->21; AV-204 22->23; AV-207 24->25), each confined to the stone; the four plain-silver pieces (AV-203/205/206/208) take no stone pass — the triage. Every piece is then reframed card-excluded to a centred 1:1 2048x2048 master (26-33, downscale only from 4032x3024 sources), consuming the _house frame for gemstone pieces and the _neutral frame for plain pieces. Each framed master fans into TWO isolations: a white-ground packshot via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) (34-41 => packshots_matched_x8, the eight @packshot cells) and a transparent cut-out via remove_background (42-49 => transparent_cutouts_x8). The wordmark takes a prep-before-trace tributary: remove_background white drop-out (50) -> crop_to_bounds trim (51) -> vectorize (52 => avenhurst_logo). Finally document_merge_data_layout (53) binds the CSV + the eight packshots + the wordmark into the authored .indd (8-page merged doc), which document_render_layout (54) exports to one press PDF. The eight card-bearing graded masters (straightened then neutralised, the outputs of 2-25 before the card-excluding crop) are retained as graded_masters_contact_x8 for neutrality grading. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all eight packshot chains plus the vectorised mark, the template and the CSV. 54 calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed single-hero version: 54 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools, one batch upload fanning into eight dependent per-SKU chains that converge on a genuine composed endpoint (an authored-.indd two-image-column data merge exported to a press PDF). Each of the eight handheld frames is first rectified for tilt with image_auto_straighten (the only tool that rotates; the tone/colour tool cannot) before any neutralisation, so a 'straightened' claim is backed by a real rotate step. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralisations are NOT one recipe run eight times — each is a per-frame white-balance/exposure delta whose sign flips by shooting session and whose magnitude must be reasoned from that frame's in-frame grey card, with the whole set forced onto one white point and the neutral silver forced true across every frame, so the naive move of applying one correction to all eight visibly fails the match. On top of that sit four heterogeneous masked colour-truth decisions in different directions (rotate the blue/green/violet stones toward true within-band, but RESTRAIN the over-saturated red), a stone-vs-no-stone triage (a chroma move on a plain-silver piece tints the neutral metal), and an enclosed-vs-open negative-space triage that governs what the transparent cut-out can and cannot show. The isolation must use remove_background({backgroundColor}) to reach a clean white PDP ground and a clean alpha cut-out — the tempting select_subject->invert->fill_area path halos the edge, solids a flat plate and bricks the openings, and no attempt may be made to punch a fully-enclosed ring centre (the connector isolates the outer ground only). The wordmark demands prep-before-trace discipline. The endpoint is a real merge with two @-image columns (text-only vector merge and PDF-converted .indd both fail to bind), gated on page-count==row-count and >=300 DPI. Every step is a headless [C] connector call; no generative fill, no canvas extension, no compositing, no upscaling, no auto-tone/preset look, no layout-by-coordinates.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong decisions, not self-measurement): (1) every frame carries an 18% grey card and the acceptance test is that each card reads truly neutral with the whole set on one white point and brightness and the neutral silver reading true head-to-head, with the agent required to REPORT its per-frame temperature/tint/exposure — a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the two-session batch leaves the cool frames blue and the warm frames yellow and fails the gate; (2) the stone-vs-no-stone triage — running a colour pass on a plain-silver piece tints the neutral metal, and skipping it on a gemstone piece leaves the stone muddy; (3) the two warm reddish stones need OPPOSITE moves (restrain the over-saturated red, rotate the violet toward true) so blanket-treating them fails; (4) the merged deliverable must have page-count == CSV-row-count == 8 with each packshot placed at >=300 DPI and the wordmark bound. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: cross-asset neutralisation of eight differently-lit frames to a shared measurable card target on differing correction signs and magnitudes, which a novice cannot match by eye; constraint-reasoning around tool limits — the tilt is rectified only by image_auto_straighten (the tone/colour and crop tools cannot rotate), isolation via remove_background({backgroundColor}) not select->invert->fill, masked recolor via image_adjust_hsl (the only masked path) not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area, image placement only via a genuine two-@-image-column .indd merge, and correctly leaving a fully-enclosed ring centre carrying its neutral surround rather than trying to punch it; prep-before-trace discipline on the wordmark; and the fine-chain alpha edge. TRAP: the brief's 'clean pure-white background' and 'transparent cut-out for layering' invite the select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area knockout, which looks right but halos the edge, flattens a solid plate and bricks the open gaps; a second trap is one blanket white-balance across the batch; a third is treating the garnet and amethyst identically; a fourth is attempting to rotate the tilt with the tone/colour tool (which cannot rotate) instead of image_auto_straighten. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: every grey card neutral (tight channel spread) and its mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target on the retained card-bearing contact set, with true-neutral silver; the four stones at their true on-brand colours with metal untouched; packshots isolated on #FFFFFF at 2048x2048 sRGB and matching alpha cut-outs (open space through, enclosed centres neutral, never gated see-through); a crisp vector wordmark; and exactly one spec card per row at >=300 DPI with both image columns bound, plus the agent's per-image parameter report so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted.
